evidence: Every quantitative claim is bounded by the data and spot-checks out: 2010s duopoly 54.5% ((208+193)/736), all-time 85.5% (4894/5726), per-year 2018 partial 46.3% ((10+27)/80), China 95.0% Long March (287/302), China reliability 95.7% (289/302) — all reproduce the inlined matrix.

The level gap is NAMED, not implied: the piece explicitly distinguishes the per-year 'crowd' from the all-time 'ledger' ('two true pictures of the same sky'), so the pluralization claim is never conflated with the unchanged cumulative record.
Partial-period flags are explicit wherever 2018 appears; the snapshot 28-27 is paired with the external full-year 39-34 and labelled 'the snapshot it is, not a final tally'.

Sample-size caveats appear where they matter: startups 92.9% 'on a thin base of 70 launches that still carries SpaceX's three early Falcon 1 failures'; the 43-attempt 'Other' bucket flagged as the lone low outlier.

Counter-evidence is kept, not hidden: 'Europe's all-time count (307) even noses ahead of China's (302)' and 'the United States never collapsed — its share even recovered' both cut against the China-rise narrative.

Third-party figures are attributed, not absorbed (cite_third_party_as_theirs_cap clear): the external full-year 2018 counts and the >$1T space-economy projection are credited to Wikipedia / CSIS in the refs, kept distinct from the project's own recomputed numbers; no causal language over correlational data.

A non-obvious reframing that updates an informed reader: the change is WHO launches, not HOW MUCH (total volume is flat-to-down, busiest year still 1967) — refuting the instinctive 'launch boom' story.

Refutes two further Cold-War reflexes with the data: the newcomers are NOT cutting corners (China's 95.7% ties the incumbents; the most reliable operators are the established commercial providers, not the startups), and the per-year crowd sits on an all-time ledger still 85.5% old-world.

Angle partly from outside the raw data (detective context): the Soviet-collapse funding cut (~80%, Buran, Baikonur stranded), the Arianespace-vs-venture-startup distinction, and the $350B->$1T space-economy stakes give the 'so what' beyond a leaderboard.

ONE clear earned hero (int_01 duel->crowd year-scrubber) that lands AT the turn (edt_03), ABOVE the reveal paragraph, so the reader PRODUCES the duopoly-share collapse rather than reading it (interaction-as-argument satisfied; not bolted on after the answer).

An EARNED supporting set (C-ABUNDANCE flagship bar, not a widget-pile): int_02 all-time ledger, int_03 annualize-the-caveat, int_04 success-rate calculator, int_05 guess-the-Long-March-share, int_06 guess-the-startup-year — each bound to a DISTINCT producible finding and each verified working + keyboard-reachable by the Auditor in real Chrome.
